processes.name: Preboarding (accept to Day 1)
processes.summary: Moves a candidate from a signed offer in Greenhouse to a cleared, equipped and fully documented first day in Darwinbox. Covers the ATS-to-HRIS handoff, background and export-control clearance, country-specific pre-start documents, IT/identity, badge and welcome. Good looks like: nobody starts uncleared, every statutory Day-1 document is signed before access is switched on, and the hire can log in and badge in on the first morning.
processes.owner: People Ops (process), Recruiter (candidate relationship to Day 1), Trade Compliance (export clearance gate)
processes.trigger: Candidate e-signs the offer and the Greenhouse offer status moves to Accepted
outputs: Darwinbox pre-hire record created from the approved Greenhouse offer (no re-keyed comp)
Background-check result and export-control clearance record, stored separately from the I-9
Signed country document pack: contract or appointment letter, PIIA/invention assignment, statutory hire notices
Provisioned identity, laptop, badge and access bundle matching the export-clearance scope
Day-1 agenda, buddy assignment and T-ONBOARD-PLAN shared with the manager
Preboarding checklist with completion timestamps (audit trail)
processes.sla: Start date at least 10 business days after acceptance (15 for export-flagged roles, longer where notice periods apply, e.g. India 60-90 days); all contingencies cleared by Day -3

steps.label: Offer accepted in Greenhouse
steps.detail: Recruiter confirms start date, work location (which drives the country document pack) and the export-control flag on the requisition. The Greenhouse-to-Darwinbox integration fires on status change; no email handoffs.

steps.label: Create pre-hire record in Darwinbox
steps.detail: Record is built only from approved offer fields (position, level, base, bonus target, equity, cost center, legal entity, location, start date). Any mismatch with the T-OFFER-APPROVAL record goes back to the recruiter, never fixed by hand.
steps.control: Offer-to-HRIS field match before activation (feeds ON-03 SOX control)

steps.label: Complete consents and pre-hire forms
steps.detail: Candidate portal collects the background-check disclosure/authorization (standalone FCRA form; ICRAA in CA; PIPL, DPDP or PDPA consent elsewhere), personal data and emergency contact. CA hires are asked whether the emergency contact may be notified if they are arrested or detained at work (SB 294).

steps.label: Order background check
steps.detail: Order the country/role package from the vendor. CA criminal checks run only post-offer with a Fair Chance individualized assessment; China has no official criminal-record check for private employers, so verify education, employment and the prior employer's termination certificate.

steps.label: Run export-control and RPS screening
steps.detail: For export-flagged roles only, collect U.S.-person status and citizenship on the separate export form (never the I-9) and screen restricted-party lists. Decide whether a deemed export or deemed reexport license is needed and record the permitted access scope in the TCP register.
steps.control: No controlled-technology access until clearance or license is recorded; same question set for every flagged role (8 U.S.C. 1324b)

steps.label: All contingencies cleared?
steps.detail: Trade Compliance and People Ops confirm background and export status in the preboarding checklist. Anything open blocks account activation.

steps.label: Resolve issue or move start date
steps.detail: Background: run pre-adverse and adverse action steps (report, summary of rights, commonly 5 business days to respond; CA adds a written individualized assessment). Export: move the start date or start on a restricted non-controlled scope, and involve Legal before any offer withdrawal.

steps.label: Issue country contract and notice pack
steps.detail: Send via e-signature the location's pack: US PIIA with DTSA immunity notice, Rule 21F-17 carve-out and state invention notices, plus a no-prior-employer-information certification; CA LC 2810.5 and SB 294 notices; ON information statement; India appointment letter; China labor contract; Canada and Taiwan contracts. Legal-approved template versions only.
steps.control: IP/confidentiality and (ON/BC) termination clauses signed before Day 1

steps.label: Sign pack and I-9 Section 1
steps.detail: Candidate signs the pack and, for US hires, completes Form I-9 Section 1 no later than the first day of work. Right-to-work documents follow the ON-02 country flow.

steps.label: Confirm Day-1 plan and buddy
steps.detail: Manager completes the week-1 section of T-ONBOARD-PLAN, names a buddy outside the reporting line in the same site or timezone, and requests the role access bundle (EDA tools, repositories, lab) within the export scope.

steps.label: Provision identity and ship equipment
steps.detail: Okta account is created disabled from the Darwinbox feed with birthright apps plus the role bundle; repository and EDA entitlements stay inside the TCP scope. Laptop is imaged and shipped (remote) or staged at site; activation happens on Day 1 after the document check.
steps.control: Access bundle compared to export scope; activation gated on the signed-PIIA flag in Darwinbox

steps.label: Encode badge and physical access
steps.detail: Badge is encoded for general site zones only; lab and restricted zones open after EHS training and export clearance. Badge photos and biometrics need the local notice or consent (CCPA notice in CA; separate consent and a non-biometric option in China).

steps.label: Send welcome comms and keep warm
steps.detail: Welcome email with Day-1 logistics, first-week agenda and buddy intro. For long notice periods (India 60-90 days, China 30 days) schedule a touchpoint every two weeks to cut reneging.

steps.label: Day -1 readiness check passed?
steps.detail: People Ops checks the preboarding report: documents signed, contingencies cleared, account staged, laptop delivered, badge encoded, manager plan done.

steps.label: Hire ready for Day 1
steps.detail: Record hands off to ON-02 (Section 2 within 3 business days), ON-03 (hire transaction) and ON-04 (Day 1 to Day 90).

raci.activity: Country contract and statutory notice pack

controls.control: Pre-hire record fields (job, level, base, equity, cost center, entity, location) match the approved offer before activation
controls.evidence: Greenhouse approval record and Darwinbox comparison report with reviewer sign-off

controls.control: Controlled-technology entitlements and restricted-zone badge access are not activated until Trade Compliance records clearance or a license
controls.evidence: Export clearance form, TCP register entry and access ticket citing the clearance ID

controls.control: Account activation is blocked until the PIIA/confidentiality agreement is signed
controls.evidence: E-signature certificate timestamped before first login

controls.control: Background-check adverse action follows FCRA/ICRAA and CA Fair Chance steps
controls.evidence: Vendor report, dated pre-adverse and adverse notices, individualized assessment

controls.control: Weekly exception report of hires starting within 10 business days with missing documents or clearances
controls.evidence: Darwinbox preboarding exception report with resolution notes

controls.control: Only Legal-approved template versions (DTSA, Rule 21F-17, state invention notices) are used
controls.evidence: Template version log and e-signature template library audit

kpis.name: Day-1 readiness (laptop, login, badge working on first morning)
kpis.why: The most visible signal of operational quality to a new hire and manager

kpis.name: Accept-to-start reneges
kpis.why: Long notice periods and counteroffers make preboarding engagement a retention lever

kpis.name: Contingencies cleared by Day -3
kpis.why: Late clearance forces start-date moves or restricted starts

kpis.name: Hires with all statutory documents signed before first login
kpis.why: Unsigned IP or termination terms are hard or impossible to fix after start

kpis.name: Week-1 new-hire experience score (T-ONBOARD-PULSE item)
kpis.why: Early indicator of first-year attrition

considerations: Set a hard minimum lead time and do not let managers pull start dates in for export-flagged roles: deemed export licenses can take weeks or months, and a restricted-scope start is better than an uncleared one.
Keep export questions off the I-9, ask them only for flagged roles with the approved U.S.-person script, and store the answers in the export record, not the personnel file.

Contracts must be signed before start: in Canada, termination, IP and restrictive terms signed after Day 1 need fresh consideration; in China the written contract is due within one month, but sign on Day 1 anyway.

Global templates break locally: no non-competes or relocation repayment in CA, no non-competes below the C-suite in Ontario, post-employment non-competes void in India, and China/Taiwan non-competes only with paid compensation for eligible roles.

Run a clean-hire protocol for hires from direct competitors (e.g., TSMC, MediaTek, Entity List companies): written no-prior-materials certification, no personal devices carrying former-employer data, and a scoped first project where needed.

Create accounts disabled and activate on Day 1. Pre-start access to repositories before the PIIA is signed is a trade-secret gap, and pre-start e-learning for non-exempt hires is compensable work time.
Collect China candidate data only after the PIPL notice and separate consent for transfer to Darwinbox/US HQ; India DPDP and CA CCPA notices at collection apply too.
Hiring into a new US state or Canadian province needs payroll, UI and tax registrations before the first payroll; Quebec remote hires need French documents and legal review first.
Karnataka now bans keeping original certificates: verify originals at the joining desk and return them the same day.

variations.how: Reactivate the existing Darwinbox ID, check rehire eligibility (OF-10), re-run background checks if the gap is over 6 months, and use I-9 Supplement B if rehired within 3 years of the original I-9 and still authorized.
E-Verify and a Form I-983 training plan are required; since the Sept 15, 2026 fixed-admission rule, build start-date buffers for I-539 and I-765 approvals.

variations.when: Sponsored foreign national (H-1B transfer, Canada work permit, Taiwan WDA permit, China work permit)
variations.how: The start date is gated by the immigration case (TA-07); no work before the permit is in hand, and payroll starts on the approved date only.
Start on a documented non-controlled scope with repository ACLs set accordingly, or defer the start; Trade Compliance signs off the scope.
Add Section 16 insider onboarding (Form 3 within 10 days), clawback policy acknowledgment, D&O questionnaire and a Form 8-K Item 5.02 check with Legal.
Load records in bulk with 100% reconciliation to the deal census, keep the acquired I-9 decision with Legal, and issue country documents in waves before integration day.

countries.us: Collect I-9 Section 1 by the first day of work and hand off to ON-02; report new hires to the state within 20 days and register withholding, UI and PFML in any new remote work state before the first payroll. The PIIA needs the DTSA immunity notice, a Rule 21F-17 protected-rights carve-out and state invention-assignment notices (e.g., IL, MN, WA, DE, NJ, NY). Background checks require a standalone FCRA disclosure, a pre-adverse notice with the report and summary of rights, a wait (commonly 5 business days), then adverse action; give NY/CT/DE electronic-monitoring notices where applicable.
countries.us-ca: Give non-exempt hires the LC 2810.5 Wage Theft Prevention Act notice, plus the SB 294 Workplace Know Your Rights notice at hire and the emergency-contact designation asking whether that contact may be notified if the employee is arrested or detained at work (LC 1550 et seq.). The PIIA must include the LC 2870 carve-out notice, and offer documents may not contain a non-compete (B&P 16600), a non-CA law or forum clause (LC 925) or relocation/training repayment terms (AB 692, agreements from 1 Jan 2026). Also give the CCPA notice at collection, CRD harassment pamphlet, SDI and PFL brochures and workers' comp pamphlet, and file the EDD DE 34 new-hire report within 20 days.
countries.ca: In Ontario (25+ employees), give the written new-hire information statement (legal and operating name, contact details, work location, starting pay, pay period and payday, anticipated hours) before Day 1 where practicable, and the ESA poster plus disconnecting-from-work and electronic-monitoring policies within 30 days. The Canadian contract (ESA-compliant termination clause, IP assignment with moral-rights waiver, equity language covering the notice period) must be signed before the start date or it needs fresh consideration. Collect the SIN within 3 days of starting plus TD1 and TD1ON/TD1BC forms, and give BC relocating hires interim cover for the MSP waiting period.
countries.in: Issue the statutory appointment letter at joining (OSH Code s.6(1)(f)) showing designation, worker or non-worker category, wages meeting the 50% 'wages' rule, PF/ESI/gratuity, notice, probation and hours, and pay Karnataka e-stamp duty on the employment agreement at execution. Background verification needs written consent, with Aadhaar voluntary and masked, and Karnataka's 2026 amendment bars keeping original certificates. Pre-collect Form 11 and UAN details (EPF mandatory up to INR 25,000/month from 17 Sep 2026) and the tax-regime choice so Day-1 payroll setup is clean.
countries.tw: Enroll Labor Insurance, Employment Insurance, Occupational Accident Insurance and NHI effective the first day of work at the correct insured-salary grade, and report the 6% labor pension within 7 days; late enrollment makes the employer liable for lost benefits. The contract (with a Traditional Chinese version) should cover the Enforcement Rules Art. 7 terms, name the employer as author of work-made copyrights (Copyright Act Art. 11) and address service-invention remuneration (Patent Act Art. 7). Run the clean-hire certification for hires from TSMC, MediaTek or UMC and arrange the employer-paid pre-employment health exam.
countries.cn: Sign the written labor contract (Chinese or bilingual, Chinese prevailing) on or before Day 1 and never later than one month after start, or double wages accrue from month 2 (LCL Arts. 10, 82). Give the PIPL employee notice and obtain separate consent for sensitive PI and for transfer to Darwinbox/US HQ, and collect the prior employer's termination certificate and check existing non-compete obligations (LCL Art. 91 joint liability). Register social insurance and housing fund within 30 days in Shanghai or Shenzhen and arrange pre-job occupational health exams for lab and test roles.

processes.name: Right-to-work verification
processes.summary: Verifies each hire's legal right to work in the country of employment using that country's statutory method, and tracks temporary authorizations so they are renewed or reverified before they lapse. Good looks like: zero unauthorized work, zero substantive I-9 errors, no document abuse, and no expired permit on payroll.
processes.owner: People Ops (process), Immigration (foreign-national permits), Legal (I-9 and E-Verify policy)
processes.trigger: Pre-hire record created in Darwinbox (ON-01), or a work-authorization expiry date comes within 90 days
outputs: Completed Form I-9 (Section 1, Section 2 and Supplement B when needed) and E-Verify case result
Canada SIN and work-permit record with expiry date (9-series SIN tracked)
Taiwan WDA work permit or Gold Card and ARC; China Foreigner's Work Permit and residence permit; India E visa and FRRO registration
Work-authorization expiry tickler in Darwinbox
Quarterly I-9 self-audit report with corrections
processes.sla: US: Section 2 within 3 business days of the first day of work; foreign-national permits in hand before Day 1; renewal or reverification started 90 days before expiry

steps.label: Hire record triggers RTW checklist
steps.detail: Darwinbox assigns the right-to-work checklist by country of employment; sponsored hires are flagged from the TA-07 immigration case, not by asking about citizenship.

steps.label: Complete Section 1 / submit documents
steps.detail: US hires complete I-9 Section 1 by the first day of work and choose any acceptable List A or List B+C documents; staff never specify documents. Elsewhere the employee provides the SIN (within 3 days of start), permit, passport or ARC.

steps.label: Foreign national needing a permit?
steps.detail: Based on the immigration flag and documents presented for the country of employment.

steps.label: Confirm permit valid before start
steps.detail: Check the permit covers this employer, occupation and location; record the expiry in Darwinbox. No start date is confirmed until the permit is in hand (Canada, Taiwan, China) or the petition allows work (US).
steps.control: Start date locked until permit recorded

steps.label: Examine documents (Section 2)
steps.detail: US: physically examine originals within 3 business days, or use the DHS remote alternative procedure (live video, copies retained, box checked) only at E-Verify sites in good standing and consistently for all hires at that site. Other countries: verify originals and record the check.

steps.label: Create E-Verify case (US, if enrolled)
steps.detail: Create the case by the third business day where E-Verify is used or required. On a tentative nonconfirmation, notify the employee privately and follow referral steps exactly; take no adverse action while the case is open.

steps.label: Resolve TNCs, lapses and audit findings
steps.detail: Legal handles suspicious documents, TNC outcomes and authorization lapses (remove from work, unpaid leave pending renewal, or separation). A quarterly I-9 self-audit corrects errors with dated, initialed annotations and no backdating.

steps.label: Diarize expiry and reverify
steps.detail: Darwinbox alerts at 90/60/30 days. Reverify in Supplement B on or before expiry only for temporary employment authorization; never reverify US citizens, permanent residents or List B identity documents.

steps.label: Authorization renewed in time?
steps.detail: Immigration confirms an extension, new permit or qualifying pending filing before the expiry date.

steps.label: RTW record complete and filed
steps.detail: Documents stored separately from the personnel file; I-9 retained for the later of 3 years after hire or 1 year after termination.

raci.activity: TNCs, lapses and quarterly I-9 audit

controls.control: Weekly report of hires without Section 2 completed within 3 business days
controls.evidence: Darwinbox I-9 timeliness report with follow-up notes

controls.control: Scripted document instructions: the employee chooses documents, and the remote procedure is applied to all hires at a site or none
controls.evidence: I-9 SOP, reviewer training log, site election record

controls.control: Monthly report of authorizations expiring within 90 days
controls.evidence: Expiry report with actions and renewal evidence

controls.control: Quarterly sample audit of I-9s and E-Verify cases
controls.evidence: Audit workpaper and annotated corrections

kpis.name: Section 2 completed within 3 business days
kpis.why: Late Section 2 is a substantive violation

kpis.name: Substantive I-9 error rate in quarterly audit
kpis.why: ICE's Mar 2026 guidance treats many former technical errors as uncurable

kpis.name: Work authorizations lapsed while on payroll
kpis.why: Unauthorized work creates penalties and immigration consequences

considerations: Keep right-to-work and export-control screening separate: the I-9 confirms work authorization only, and linking the two invites citizenship discrimination and document-abuse charges.
Over-verification is document abuse: asking a green-card holder to reverify, or demanding a specific document, breaches 8 U.S.C. 1324b even when well meant.
Audit before an inspection, not after: ICE's Mar 2026 guidance leaves no cure period for many errors, so the quarterly self-audit is the only realistic fix window.
Use an authorized representative for remote hires at sites that do not use E-Verify; the remote alternative procedure is only for E-Verify employers in good standing.
Store I-9s and permit copies separately from personnel files with restricted access, and purge on schedule.

variations.when: Rehire within 3 years of the original I-9
variations.how: Use Supplement B (rehire) if the employee is still authorized; otherwise complete a new I-9.
E-Verify is mandatory, the I-983 training plan and reporting apply, and fixed I-94 end dates (from Sept 15, 2026) must be tracked alongside the EAD.
Legal decides whether to retain the seller's I-9s (inheriting their errors) or complete new I-9s for everyone, and applies the choice consistently.
Run the destination country's check from scratch; the permit must be in hand before the first working day there.

countries.us: Form I-9 Section 1 by the first day of work and Section 2 within 3 business days, on the 01/20/25 edition (the 08/01/23 print expiring 07/31/2026 may not be used), with remote examination only for E-Verify employers in good standing; ICE's Mar 2026 guidance makes many former technical errors substantive ($288-$2,861 per form). E-Verify applies under the FAR clause, state mandates (e.g., AZ, AL, MS, SC, GA, NC 25+, FL 25+, UT 150+) and for STEM OPT hires.
countries.us-ca: Use E-Verify only as federal law requires, never before an offer or to check current employees, and notify employees within 72 hours of a federal I-9 inspection notice (LC 1019.1, 1019.2, 90.2). Do not let immigration agents into non-public areas without a judicial warrant (Gov Code 7285.1-7285.2).
countries.ca: Collect the SIN within 3 days of starting and record the permit expiry for 9-series SINs, which expire with the permit; for LMIA-exempt hires submit the offer in the IRCC Employer Portal with the C$230 fee and keep records 6 years. Keep wages and duties consistent with the permit conditions (IRPR ss.209.2-209.3).
countries.in: Indian nationals need no permit check, so confirm identity through consented background verification (Aadhaar voluntary and masked) and return original certificates the same day (Karnataka 2026 amendment). Foreign nationals need an Employment (E) visa (generally salary over USD 25,000/yr) and FRRO registration within 14 days of arrival if staying 180+ days, under the Immigration and Foreigners Act 2025 (verify employer reporting duties).
countries.tw: Foreign professionals need a WDA work permit for specialized work (salary threshold currently NT$47,971/month; verify) or an Employment Gold Card, plus an ARC, before starting; 2026 amendments widened eligibility for top-university graduates. Never hold employees' passports or ID cards (Employment Services Act).
countries.cn: Foreign hires need the Foreigner's Work Permit (A/B/C tier), a Z visa and a residence permit within 30 days of entry before working, and foreign contracts run at most 5 years; SPC Interpretation II Art. 4 recognizes employment only for foreigners with PR or valid permits. Taiwan-resident engineers can work in the mainland without a PRC work permit, but check their Taiwan obligations (e.g., core key technology travel approvals) first.

processes.name: Hire transaction & HRIS setup
processes.summary: Turns the pre-hire record into an active Darwinbox worker with the correct position, cost center, legal entity, compensation and payroll attributes, sourced only from the approved offer. It is a SOX control point because the hire record feeds payroll, equity grants and headcount reporting. Good looks like: every record matches the approved offer, a second person reviews it before the first payroll cut-off, and the audit trail is complete.
processes.owner: People Ops (process and data), Payroll (payroll acceptance), Finance (cost center and SOX control owner)
processes.trigger: Preboarding contingencies cleared (ON-01), or Day 1 for same-week starts
outputs: Active Darwinbox worker record linked to an approved, budgeted position
Compensation record (base, currency, bonus target, allowances, sign-on) matching the approved offer
Payroll new-hire interface record with statutory IDs (SSN, SIN, UAN, ARC, SI/HF numbers)
New-hire equity grant request queued for Stock Admin (EQ-01)
Maker-checker approval log and audit trail retained for SOX testing
processes.sla: Hire entered and approved by Day -3, and always before the input cut-off of the first pay period

steps.label: Contingencies cleared; hire ready
steps.detail: ON-01 checklist shows background, export and document steps complete, so the hire transaction can be finalized.

steps.label: Link hire to approved position
steps.detail: Select the open position from PL-02; it carries job code, level, overtime classification, location, legal entity, cost center and manager. No approved position, no hire.

steps.label: Load comp from approved offer
steps.detail: Base, currency, pay frequency, bonus target, sign-on and allowances flow through the Greenhouse integration; manual entry needs a ticket with the approved offer attached. Check exempt status against the salary floor for the location.
steps.control: Comp fields locked to integration values; manual overrides logged

steps.label: Enter statutory and payroll data
steps.detail: Tax forms (W-4 and state, TD1, India regime election, China IIT deductions), bank details, statutory IDs, work state or social-insurance city, and worker/special-hours classification.

steps.label: Maker-checker review
steps.detail: A second People Ops reviewer compares the record to the approved offer and position: job, level, base, bonus target, cost center, entity, location and start date. Darwinbox roles stop a maker approving their own entry.
steps.control: Key SOX control: independent review of new-hire record

steps.label: Record matches the offer?
steps.detail: Checker approves or rejects with a reason code.

steps.label: Accept new hire into payroll
steps.detail: Payroll reviews the new-hire interface report against Darwinbox, confirms first-period proration and any new state, province or city registration before cut-off; mismatches go back to People Ops.

steps.label: Queue new-hire equity grant
steps.detail: Equity from the offer is queued for the next scheduled grant date under the equity grant policy; share count is set at grant under the approved conversion method and approved by the Comp Committee or its delegate.

steps.label: Reconcile hires to headcount and GL
steps.detail: Monthly, Finance reconciles new hires to approved positions and cost centers and new-hire pay to the GL; any unexplained hire is investigated.
steps.control: Detective reconciliation of hires to approved positions

steps.label: Hire active; audit trail retained
steps.detail: Transaction history, approvals and source documents stay in Darwinbox for SOX testing and record retention.

controls.control: Independent review of each new-hire record against the approved offer before the first payroll
controls.evidence: Darwinbox approval log with maker and checker IDs, timestamps and attached offer

controls.control: Segregation of duties: no single user can create a worker, change pay and approve payroll
controls.evidence: Quarterly user-access review (DS-04)

controls.control: Monthly exception report of Darwinbox comp vs Greenhouse approved offers
controls.evidence: Report with completeness and accuracy (IPE) evidence and reviewer sign-off

controls.control: Monthly reconciliation of new hires to approved positions and the payroll register
controls.evidence: Reconciliation workpaper signed by Finance

kpis.name: Hire records matching the approved offer at first review
kpis.why: Measures input quality at the source of payroll data

kpis.name: New hires paid correctly on first payroll
kpis.why: First-paycheck errors damage trust and trigger off-cycles

kpis.name: Hires entered before first payroll cut-off
kpis.why: Late entry forces off-cycle payments

kpis.name: SOX exceptions in hire controls
kpis.why: Hire-to-pay is in audit scope

considerations: Integrate, do not retype: comp fields should come from the approved Greenhouse offer, with manual edits the logged exception.

Classification set at hire drives overtime exposure: CA exempt floors, Taiwan's lack of any salary-based exemption, India 'worker' status and China special-hours approval should be position attributes, not individual guesses.
The legal employer (US corp, Canadian subsidiary, India private limited, Taiwan entity, China WFOE) determines payroll, tax and social-insurance registration; a wrong entity is expensive to unwind.
Reports used in the review control need completeness and accuracy evidence (parameters, record counts), because auditors test the report as well as the review.
A hire entered after cut-off still has to be paid on time (CA non-exempt within 7 days of period close), so route it to PY-02 rather than deferring wages.

variations.how: Enter as pending, keep checker review before any payment, and use an off-cycle (PY-02) if the cut-off is missed.
Reactivate the original ID to preserve service history (Canada notice, Taiwan seniority, China cumulative service for annual leave) and attach a new position.
Close the contingent or intern record, create a new hire record, and re-check classification (MV-05).
Migrate with 100% record-count and pay-total reconciliation and a sample-based checker review agreed in advance with auditors.

countries.us: Capture work state and city for withholding, UI, PFML and local tax, W-4 and state forms, and FLSA exempt status against the $684/week floor and higher state thresholds; report new hires to the state within 20 days.
countries.us-ca: Mark a role exempt only if it meets $70,304 (2026) or the computer-professional $58.85/hr ($122,573.13/yr) and the duties test; technicians and lab operators default to non-exempt. Capture the data needed for LC 226 wage statements and the EDD DE 34 new-hire report within 20 days.
countries.ca: Enter SIN, TD1 and TD1ON/TD1BC, province of employment (drives CPP/EI, EHT and WSIB or WorkSafeBC) and hours-of-work exemption status (ON IT professional; BC high-technology professional, ESR s.37.8), plus the 4% or 6% vacation pay basis.
countries.in: Record worker vs non-worker status (supervisor ceiling INR 18,000), a CTC split where 'wages' are at least 50% of remuneration, UAN/ESIC numbers and the tax-regime election, plus the state (Karnataka or Telangana) for PT and LWF.
countries.tw: Record insured-salary grades for Labor Insurance and NHI and the pension wage grade (6% employer contribution) effective Day 1, resident vs non-resident tax status (183-day rule; 18% non-resident withholding) and the statutory roster fields (LSA Art. 7).
countries.cn: Record contract term and probation end date (LCL Art. 19 limits and fixed-term counting), social-insurance and housing-fund city and base, IIT special additional deductions and any special working-hours approval; for foreigners, record permit numbers and the allowance-vs-deduction election.

processes.name: Day 1 to Day 90 onboarding & probation
processes.summary: Takes a new hire from Day-1 orientation through mandatory training and policy acknowledgments, structured 30/60/90 check-ins and, where it applies, a documented probation review with a confirmation, extension or exit decision. Good looks like: all acknowledgments and training done within 30 days (CA harassment within 6 months), three documented check-ins for every hire, and probation decisions made on time with evidence that holds up locally.
processes.owner: Manager (ramp and probation recommendation), HRBP (probation decision quality), People Ops (Day 1, tracking, letters), L&D (curriculum)
processes.trigger: Employee's first day of work (Darwinbox status Active)
outputs: Signed acknowledgments: Code of Conduct, Insider Trading Policy, IP/confidentiality, acceptable use, local handbook or work rules
LMS completion records for compliance training (harassment/POSH, insider trading, export/TCP, EHS)
30/60/90 check-in records in the Performance module against T-ONBOARD-PLAN
T-ONBOARD-PULSE results at Day 30 and Day 90
Probation review and confirmation, extension or non-confirmation letter where probation applies
Onboarding completion status in Darwinbox
processes.sla: Acknowledgments within 5 business days; mandatory training within 30 days (CA harassment within 6 months); probation decision at least 10 business days before probation ends

steps.label: Day 1: activate and orient
steps.detail: Accounts are activated after the document check; orientation covers the company, security and trade-secret rules and speak-up channels. Day-1 statutory items (I-9 Section 2, SIN, bank and tax forms) are collected.

steps.label: Sign policy acknowledgments
steps.detail: E-sign the Code of Conduct, Insider Trading Policy (blackouts, pre-clearance, designated-insider status), acceptable use and monitoring notice, and the local handbook or work rules (China handbook adopted through democratic procedure; Taiwan filed work rules).
steps.control: Code and insider-trading acknowledgments required before equity portal and pre-clearance access

steps.label: Assign compliance curriculum
steps.detail: LMS assigns by country and role: Code and insider trading for all; TCP briefing for export-flagged roles; EHS before lab access; CA harassment; India POSH; Taiwan OSH; Ontario AODA and OHS awareness.
steps.control: Lab badge zones open only after EHS completion (LMS-to-badge feed)

steps.label: Kick off 30/60/90 plan
steps.detail: Manager and hire agree the T-ONBOARD-PLAN outcomes, first deliverables (e.g., own a verification block or a test program), stakeholders and tools. Where probation applies, write down measurable confirmation criteria and get them acknowledged (required in China).

steps.label: Complete mandatory training
steps.detail: Employee completes the curriculum with LMS reminders at Day 14 and Day 25; overdue items escalate to the manager at Day 30. For non-exempt staff, training time is paid time.

steps.label: Day-30 check-in
steps.detail: Record progress against the plan, access or tool gaps and early concerns in the Performance module. Any performance concern must be written down specifically now, because CN, TW and IN decisions depend on it later.

steps.label: Send Day-30 pulse; chase overdue
steps.detail: Send T-ONBOARD-PULSE (role clarity, tools, manager, buddy, belonging) and the overdue-training report to managers and HRBPs. Results are reported only for groups of 5 or more.

steps.label: Day-60 check-in
steps.detail: Mid-point feedback; for probation roles, a documented mid-probation review with specific examples measured against the disclosed criteria.

steps.label: Day-90 review and recommendation
steps.detail: Structured review against the plan, with a recommendation to confirm, extend or not confirm where probation applies; in the US it is a check-in with no 'permanent status' language.

steps.label: Probation outcome?
steps.detail: HRBP tests the recommendation against evidence, consistency across similar hires and the country rules before anything is communicated.

steps.label: Issue extension with plan
steps.detail: Extend only where the contract and local law allow (typically once in India); China probation cannot exceed the statutory maximum and is allowed only once per employer; in Canada extension does not delay the 3-month ESA threshold. The letter restates the criteria and the new review date.

steps.label: Review non-confirmation exit
steps.detail: Legal and Employee Relations review evidence and local rules before any exit and route it to OF-02. China needs proof of failing disclosed criteria, notice before probation ends and prior union notification; Taiwan needs an LSA Art. 11 ground.
steps.control: Legal sign-off required for every non-confirmation outside the US

steps.label: Issue confirmation letter
steps.detail: Send the confirmation letter by e-signature where used (India standard practice; optional elsewhere) and update the Darwinbox probation status, which triggers any confirmation-linked benefits or notice terms.

steps.label: Complete Day-90 pulse
steps.detail: Employee completes the Day-90 T-ONBOARD-PULSE; results feed HR Analytics and manager coaching.

steps.label: Close onboarding record
steps.detail: Onboarding status closes in Darwinbox; the employee moves into PD-01 goal setting, or the case moves to OF-02 for a non-confirmation.

controls.evidence: E-signature records by employee and access provisioning log

controls.control: Training completion tracked against statutory deadlines (CA 6 months, POSH at induction, AODA as soon as practicable)
controls.evidence: LMS completion report with SB 513 fields; CA certificates kept 2 years

controls.control: Lab and restricted-zone access opens only after EHS training
controls.evidence: LMS-to-badge integration log

controls.evidence: Darwinbox alert log and decision record

controls.control: Legal review of every non-confirmation outside the US before communication
controls.evidence: Legal sign-off in the ER case file

controls.control: TCP briefing acknowledgment for export-flagged employees before controlled access
controls.evidence: Signed TCP acknowledgment linked to the clearance record

kpis.name: Mandatory training completed within 30 days
kpis.why: Missed statutory training is a direct compliance failure

kpis.name: 30/60/90 check-ins documented
kpis.why: Documented check-ins drive ramp and are evidence in probation decisions

kpis.name: Probation decisions recorded before the end date
kpis.why: Missed dates lose the probation window (China) or trigger notice rights (Canada)

kpis.name: Voluntary attrition within 90 days
kpis.why: Early exits usually trace back to onboarding or role mismatch

kpis.name: Day-90 pulse: role clarity and manager support
kpis.why: Leading indicator of first-year retention

kpis.name: Manager rates hire fully contributing at Day 90
kpis.why: Measures time to productivity

considerations: In the US avoid 'probation' language that implies permanent status after it ends; call it an introductory period and say it does not change at-will employment.

China probation is the only cheap exit window but it is narrow: criteria disclosed and acknowledged at hire, evidence gathered during probation, and the decision notified before probation expires. Diarize at contract signature, not at Day 80.

Taiwan has no statutory probation; ending employment at the end of an agreed probation still needs an LSA Art. 11 or 12 ground, and Art. 16 notice applies once tenure reaches 3 months, so decide before month 3 where you can.
Canada: ESA notice and BC compensation for length of service start after 3 months, and a probation clause only limits notice if it says so clearly. Assess suitability in good faith and document it.
India: state in the contract whether confirmation is automatic at the end of probation, and diarize the date to avoid disputes over 'deemed confirmation'; notice periods often change on confirmation.

Brief engineers on insider trading in week 1: people who see design wins, customer forecasts or tape-out results may be designated insiders, and 'shadow trading' in customer or competitor stock is a live risk (SEC v. Panuwat).
Pulse anonymity matters at small sites (e.g., a handful of Hsinchu hires a quarter): report results by quarter or region once n is at least 5.
Remind competitor hires at Day 30 of the clean-hire certification; in Taiwan, misuse of national core key technology carries criminal exposure for the individual and the company.
Taiwan's 2026 sick-leave rule bars adverse appraisal for up to 10 sick days a year, so probation reviews must not count protected sick leave against the hire.

variations.how: Virtual orientation and shipped equipment; add ON disconnecting-from-work and monitoring policies, CA LC 2802 reimbursement setup and a buddy in the same timezone.
Cohort orientation and a shortened 30/60 plan; interns have no probation, and the conversion decision feeds TA-08.
Adds the CA 2-hour supervisor harassment course, manager essentials training and briefings on POSH IC and speak-up escalation duties.
EHS, chemical hygiene and HazCom training before lab access, occupational health exams in China and Taiwan, and shift and overtime rules briefing (PY-03).
Section 16 onboarding (Form 3 within 10 days), pre-clearance setup, clawback acknowledgment and D&O questionnaire alongside the standard plan.

variations.when: Rehire or transfer with prior service
variations.how: Check whether prior service counts (Canada notice, Taiwan seniority, China cumulative service) and whether a new probation is allowed (China: once per employer).

variations.when: Hire who reports a concern during onboarding
variations.how: Route to ER-01 immediately and keep the probation decision separate, with Legal review to avoid any retaliation inference.

countries.us: There is no statutory probation; any introductory period should state it does not change at-will status (Montana's WDEA probation is the exception). State harassment-training deadlines follow the work location: NY at hire and annually, CT 2 hours within 6 months (3+ employees), DE within 1 year (50+), ME within 1 year (15+), IL annually. Benefits waiting periods may not exceed 90 days (ACA).
countries.us-ca: Complete 1-hour (non-supervisor) or 2-hour (supervisor) interactive harassment training within 6 months of hire or promotion and keep records 2 years (Gov Code 12950.1), and record SB 513 training details (trainer, date, duration, competencies). Deliver IIPP orientation, WVPP training, HazCom and lab chemical hygiene training before lab work. Keep any introductory period explicitly at-will; the PSL 90-day use wait runs on its own schedule.
countries.ca: There is no statutory probation, but ON ESA notice and BC compensation for length of service start only after 3 months' service, so complete and document the review before month 3; a contractual probation clause must clearly limit notice or common-law reasonable notice applies. Ontario hires need AODA training as soon as practicable and basic OHS awareness training; BC hires need new and young worker orientation before starting work.
countries.in: There is no statutory probation limit; market practice is 3-6 months, extendable once, closed with a written confirmation letter, and where standing orders apply (300+ workers) their probation terms govern workers. Deliver POSH awareness at induction and keep acknowledgments of standing orders or service rules, the privacy notice and the acceptable-use policy.
countries.tw: Probation is not statutory; an agreed period (commonly 3 months) does not allow free exit, since termination still needs an LSA Art. 11 or 12 ground, Art. 16 notice once tenure reaches 3 months, and pro-rated severance. Deliver general OSH training (typically at least 3 hours) and the work rules, with harassment and (from 1 July 2026) workplace-bullying complaint channels acknowledged.
countries.cn: Probation is capped by contract term: 1 month (3 months to under 1 year), 2 months (1 to under 3 years), 6 months (3+ years or open-ended), once per employee per employer, at no less than 80% of the agreed wage and the local minimum (LCL Arts. 19-20). Termination during probation (Art. 39(1)) needs evidence of failing pre-disclosed, acknowledged hiring criteria, notice before probation expires and prior union notification (Art. 43).

processes.name: Relocation
processes.summary: Provides relocation support for new hires and employees asked to move, domestically or internationally, with correct payroll tax treatment and repayment terms that are lawful where the employee works. Good looks like: tiered, pre-approved packages; costs imputed and grossed up in the right payroll period; immigration and start dates aligned; and no repayment clause that is void in the destination location.
processes.owner: Mobility (process and vendor), Total Rewards (package design), Payroll (tax reporting), Legal (repayment agreements)
processes.trigger: Approved offer or internal move (MV-01, MV-03) that includes a relocation benefit
outputs: Relocation authorization with tier, budget and gross-up decision
Signed country-specific relocation agreement (repayment terms only where lawful)
Vendor initiation and move plan (household goods, temporary housing, home-finding, destination services)
Payroll imputation and gross-up records per country
Cost reconciliation and closure record
processes.sla: Authorization within 3 business days of offer approval; vendor contact within 2 business days of initiation; costs imputed in the pay period they are paid

steps.label: Relocation approved in offer or move
steps.detail: Mobility receives the approved offer or transfer with the relocation line item and destination.

steps.label: Assign tier and estimate true cost
steps.detail: Tier by level and move type (domestic lump sum, domestic managed, international). The estimate includes gross-up so Finance sees the full cost; anything above tier needs Total Rewards and Dept Head approval.

steps.label: International move?
steps.detail: Cross-border moves need immigration sequencing before any lease or shipment is committed.

steps.label: Align permit, family and start date
steps.detail: Work permit before start (TA-07/MV-06), dependant permits checked (Canada spousal open work permits now limited), and the export status re-screened for the new site. Shipping and lease dates follow visa approval, not the reverse.

steps.label: Issue country relocation agreement
steps.detail: Use the destination template: no repayment clause for CA agreements from 1 Jan 2026 (AB 692); a pro-rated, cost-linked clawback in India; no liquidated damages in China beyond training and non-compete cases.
steps.control: Only Legal-approved country templates; CA template has no repayment clause

steps.label: Sign agreement and start move
steps.detail: Employee e-signs, meets the vendor and submits receipts for accountable items; lump sums are paid through payroll, not AP.

steps.label: Impute, withhold and gross up
steps.detail: Taxable relocation is imputed in the period paid, with the approved gross-up covering income and payroll taxes; vendor-paid items are reported monthly so nothing escapes the W-2, T4 or local equivalent.
steps.control: Monthly vendor spend vs imputed income reconciliation

steps.label: Leaver within repayment period?
steps.detail: Checked at termination (OF-01/OF-02) against the signed agreement and the law of the work location.

steps.label: Recover per agreement (PY-05)
steps.detail: Recover the pro-rated amount by invoice or by payroll deduction only with written authorization and within local limits; never from CA final pay.

steps.label: Reconcile costs and close
steps.detail: Vendor invoices reconciled to the authorization, year-end tax reconciliation done for moves spanning two tax years, and the file closed.

controls.control: Country-specific relocation templates approved by Legal; CA template contains no repayment clause
controls.evidence: Template version log and Legal approval record

controls.control: Monthly reconciliation of vendor-reported relocation spend to income imputed in payroll
controls.evidence: Signed reconciliation workpaper

controls.control: Spend above tier requires documented Total Rewards and Dept Head approval
controls.evidence: Exception approval ticket

controls.control: Payroll recovery only with signed authorization and a lawful clause
controls.evidence: Authorization linked to the deduction code

kpis.name: Relocation costs imputed in the correct pay period
kpis.why: Late imputation causes W-2c/amended slips and under-withholding

kpis.name: Moves within approved tier budget
kpis.why: Controls cost creep from exceptions

kpis.name: Start dates slipped due to relocation or immigration
kpis.why: Signals sequencing problems

kpis.name: Relocating employee satisfaction
kpis.why: Relocation experience shapes early engagement

considerations: Gross-ups can add half again to the taxable cost; decide gross-up policy by tier and prefer lump sums sized on a net basis for junior moves.
After AB 692, design CA retention with forward vesting (RSUs, deferred cash earned over time) instead of relocation clawbacks.
A move can change export status: a foreign national moving to a US or Canadian site may need a new deemed export or reexport assessment before access is restored.
Mobile employees create split-sourced RSU income across states and countries; tell Stock Admin and Payroll the move date before the next vest.
China transfers between Shanghai and Shenzhen need written consent (LCL Art. 35), and Taiwan transfers must meet the LSA Art. 10-1 principles, including help with the location change.

variations.when: Domestic lump sum (default for junior hires)
variations.how: Single payroll payment, taxable, no vendor; no repayment clause in CA.
A permanent move (MV-03) localizes to the host payroll; an assignment (MV-02) stays home-based with shadow payroll and tax equalization.
Mobility settles sunk costs (lease breaks, storage) and Payroll still imputes taxable amounts already paid.
Track relocation and any tax gross-up as perquisites for proxy disclosure; investors and proxy advisors view gross-ups critically.

countries.us: Relocation payments and reimbursements are taxable wages for non-military employees (the IRC 132(g) exclusion suspension was made permanent by OBBBA; verify), withheld as supplemental wages at 22% (37% over $1M) and reported on the W-2. Outside CA, repayment agreements are generally enforceable, but payroll deductions must follow state deduction laws (e.g., NY Labor Law 193) and cannot take a non-exempt employee below minimum wage.
countries.us-ca: For agreements entered on or after 1 Jan 2026, employers cannot require repayment of relocation, training or similar costs when employment ends (AB 692; B&P 16608, LC 926), with $5,000 minimum damages per worker; only narrow exceptions remain, and AB 1697 may change the scope or timing (verify). Reimburse necessary business expenses under LC 2802.
countries.ca: Spousal open work permits are limited to spouses of TEER 0/1 (or listed TEER 2/3) workers with 16+ months left on the permit, and BC's MSP waiting period (rest of the arrival month plus 2 months) needs interim private cover. Employer-paid moves are taxable unless they qualify as non-taxable reimbursed moving expenses under CRA rules (verify), and repayment deductions from wages need written authorization (ON ESA s.13; BC ESA ss.21-22).
countries.in: Joining-bonus and relocation clawbacks are enforceable only as reasonable liquidated damages tied to actual cost and pro-rated (Indian Contract Act s.74; Vijaya Bank v. Prashant Narnaware, 2025). Recovery from final pay needs clear contract terms and must stay within Code on Wages s.18 authorised deductions (50% cap).
countries.tw: Minimum-service commitments must be in writing and are valid only where the employer funded special training or pays reasonable compensation for the commitment (LSA Art. 15-1), so relocation alone may not support one (verify). Employer-initiated transfers must follow LSA Art. 10-1, including help with the location change and regard for family life.
countries.cn: Liquidated damages may be agreed only for training service periods and non-competes (LCL Arts. 22-23, 25), so structure any relocation clawback as a written, pro-rated refund of an advance and confirm with local counsel (verify). Foreign employees may choose tax-exempt housing, language and children's education allowances (through 31 Dec 2027) or special additional deductions, not both.

processes.name: Payroll cycle: change control & close
processes.summary: Runs every payroll cycle in every country from input cut-off to GL posting under SOX-grade change control: only approved changes go in, every master-data change is independently checked, variances are explained before approval, and payroll reconciles to the general ledger. Covers multi-country providers, statutory remittances and equity income processed through payroll. Good looks like: on-time and accurate pay, no unexplained variances, remittances made by statutory deadlines and clean SOX testing.
processes.owner: Payroll (process and control operation), Finance/Controller (SOX control owner and GL), People Ops (HRIS input quality)
processes.trigger: Country payroll calendar reaches the input cut-off (semi-monthly or biweekly US/Canada; monthly India, Taiwan, China)
outputs: Certified HRIS input and change report with evidence of review
Payroll register and gross-to-net variance analysis with explanations
Maker-checker register approval and funding authorization
Country-compliant payslips and wage statements (e.g., CA LC 226)
Statutory remittance confirmations (IRS/state, CRA, EPFO/ESIC/PT/TDS, BLI/NHI/pension, China SI/HF/IIT)
Payroll-to-GL and bank reconciliation with reviewer sign-off
processes.sla: Input cut-off at T-5 business days before pay date; register approved by T-2; funding T-1; GL reconciliation within 3 business days after pay date; remittances by each statutory deadline

steps.label: Cut-off reached per calendar
steps.detail: Annual country payroll calendars fix cut-off, approval, funding and pay dates. Changes after cut-off move to the next cycle or, if pay would be late, to PY-02.

steps.label: Finalize and certify HRIS changes
steps.detail: All hires, terminations, pay changes, allowances and unpaid leave are approved in Darwinbox before cut-off, and People Ops certifies the change set complete. No changes by email or spreadsheet.
steps.control: Signed cut-off certification

steps.label: Send equity income file
steps.detail: RSU releases, option exercises and ESPP purchases (including disqualifying dispositions) with FMV, shares withheld or sold to cover and tax jurisdiction per employee, reconciled to the equity platform release report.
steps.control: Equity file tied to the platform release report before load

steps.label: Load inputs and run change report
steps.detail: Import the HRIS interface, approved time from Timekeeping, one-time payments and equity income. Generate a change report listing every new hire, termination, rate change and bank-account change since the last cycle.

steps.label: Trace changes to approved source
steps.detail: A second payroll specialist traces 100% of rate and bank changes, and a sample of other changes, to approved Darwinbox transactions. Bank changes are confirmed by call-back to a number already on file.
steps.control: Change report reviewed by someone other than the entrant; bank changes independently verified

steps.label: Calculate gross-to-net
steps.detail: Provider runs the preliminary payroll with country rules: US federal/state/local and supplemental rates; Canada CPP/CPP2/EI; India PF/ESI/PT/TDS; Taiwan LI/EI/NHI/pension; China SI/HF and cumulative IIT.

steps.label: Analyze variances vs prior cycle
steps.detail: Compare the register to the prior period by employee and cost center against set thresholds (e.g., +/-10% or a local-currency amount); flag negative nets, zero pays and pay above expected caps. Every exception gets a written explanation (vest, bonus, OT, proration).
steps.control: Key detective control: documented variance review

steps.label: All variances explained?
steps.detail: Payroll manager reviews the variance file before sending it for approval.

steps.label: Approve register and release funding
steps.detail: Payroll manager (maker) and a Finance approver (checker) sign the register summary and compare totals to the cash forecast; funding goes to the provider or bank only after approval.
steps.control: Maker-checker approval before funding

steps.label: Pay, issue payslips, remit
steps.detail: Pay on the statutory or scheduled date and issue country-compliant payslips; the provider makes statutory deposits and filings under its service agreement.

steps.label: Confirm statutory remittances
steps.detail: Track every deposit against its deadline (941 schedule, CRA remitter schedule, India TDS by the 7th and PF/ESI by the 15th, China IIT by the 15th, Taiwan monthly premiums) and file confirmations.

steps.label: Post and reconcile payroll to GL
steps.detail: Post the payroll journal and reconcile gross pay, employer taxes and withholding liabilities to the GL and bank; clear suspense items within 30 days. Reviewer signs the reconciliation.
steps.control: Payroll-to-GL reconciliation reviewed and signed

steps.label: Log issues and root-cause
steps.detail: Log errors, off-cycles and late inputs with root cause, feeding PY-02, PY-05 and the quarterly SOX deficiency assessment. Tax-table and rate changes are tested before first live use.

steps.label: Cycle closed; evidence archived
steps.detail: Change report, variance file, approvals and reconciliations are archived per cycle for SOX testing.

controls.control: Input cut-off with People Ops certification that all approved HRIS changes are complete
controls.evidence: Signed certification and cut-off log per cycle

controls.control: 100% of pay-rate and bank-account changes traced to an approved source by someone other than the entrant
controls.evidence: Annotated change report with reviewer initials and date

controls.control: Variance analysis against thresholds with written explanations
controls.evidence: Variance file with explanations and reviewer sign-off

controls.control: Maker-checker approval of the register before funding
controls.evidence: Approval record and funding instruction

controls.control: Payroll-to-GL and bank reconciliation within 3 business days
controls.evidence: Signed reconciliation workpaper

controls.control: Equity income in payroll reconciled to the equity platform each cycle
controls.evidence: Tie-out of platform release report to payroll equity earnings

controls.control: Annual review of payroll providers' SOC 1 Type II reports and operation of complementary user-entity controls
controls.evidence: SOC 1 review memo with bridge letters

controls.control: Segregation of duties: nobody can change master data and approve payroll
controls.evidence: Quarterly user-access review

kpis.name: Payroll accuracy (payslips needing no correction)
kpis.why: Core quality measure

kpis.name: On-time pay
kpis.why: Late pay triggers statutory penalties and trust damage

kpis.name: Off-cycle payments
kpis.why: Off-cycles signal upstream input failures and carry control risk

kpis.name: Statutory remittance or filing penalties
kpis.why: Direct cost and audit exposure

kpis.name: Unreconciled GL items older than 30 days
kpis.why: Aged items hide errors and fraud

kpis.name: Payroll SOX deficiencies
kpis.why: Payroll is a core ICFR area

considerations: One global calendar, local rules: CA non-exempt pay within 7 days of period close, BC within 8 days, India before the 7th, and fixed paydays in Taiwan and China. Build the calendar backwards from the strictest rule.
Equity income is the biggest variance driver: align vest dates with cut-offs, confirm sell-to-cover settlement before the run, and apply the mandatory 37% US rate above $1M of supplemental wages.
Payroll diversion fraud usually comes through bank-change requests; call back on a known number and hold same-cycle changes above a threshold.

Multi-country providers mean multiple control environments: get SOC 1 Type II reports (or agreed procedures where none exist), map the complementary user-entity controls, and do not assume the provider reviews your inputs.

Keep a rate-change calendar and test each change in parallel before first use: Jan 1 US wage base and CPP/EI rates, 1 Jan Taiwan minimum wage and grade tables, 1 Jul Shanghai SI base, 17 Sep 2026 India EPF ceiling.
India's 50% 'wages' rule (since 21 Nov 2025) changes PF and gratuity bases, so payroll configuration, not just CTC letters, must compute it.
China social insurance must be paid on the actual base; waiver agreements are void, and Shanghai's 2026 retroactive top-ups were due by 30 Sept 2026.
Small country teams cannot split duties internally; use a regional reviewer or have the provider prepare and in-house staff approve so maker-checker still holds.
Reports used in controls (change report, variance report) need IPE evidence: saved parameters, record counts and a tie-out to the register.

variations.when: New country, entity or US state
variations.how: Register tax, social-insurance and payroll accounts first (state withholding/UI/PFML, CRA RP account, EPFO/ESIC, BLI/NHI, SI/HF), then run a parallel payroll before live.

variations.when: First cycle of the calendar or tax year
variations.how: Load new tax tables and wage bases, reset annual caps (CPP/EI, SS wage base, cumulative IIT), process W-4 exemption renewals due Feb 15, and India regime elections in April.

variations.when: Bonus cycle (annual bonus, Taiwan Lunar New Year bonus, China one-off bonus)
variations.how: Run a special cycle with the bonus file approved by Total Rewards; apply the NHI 2.11% supplementary premium and the China separate-taxation choice.
Stock Admin confirms settlement and withholding before cut-off; Section 16 officers are handled with Legal for Form 4 timing.
At least two parallel runs, YTD balance conversion reconciled to the penny, and SOX walkthroughs updated before go-live.
Final-pay deadlines drive timing (CA immediate); route to PY-02 and OF-05 with a dedicated reconciliation.

variations.when: Retro pay after the annual comp review
variations.how: Retro amounts are recalculated from the approved CO-02 file and variance-checked by employee before approval.

countries.us: Withhold federal income tax (supplemental 22%, mandatory 37% over $1M, relevant to RSU vests), FICA with the $184,500 2026 Social Security wage base and 0.9% Additional Medicare over $200K, and state and local taxes by work location, depositing on the Form 941 schedule. Register each new remote work state before its first payroll and isolate the FLSA overtime premium for W-2 code TT. Keep payroll records 3 years (FLSA) and payroll tax records 4 years.
countries.us-ca: Non-exempt staff must be paid at least twice monthly, within 7 days after the period closes (LC 204), with LC 226 itemized wage statements showing gross and net wages, hours and rates, deductions, period dates, last-4 SSN or ID, legal employer name and address and PSL balance; penalties run $50 then $100 per period up to $4,000 per employee, plus PAGA. Withhold SDI at 1.3% of all wages (no cap) and include non-discretionary bonuses and shift differentials in the regular rate.
countries.ca: Withhold federal and provincial tax, CPP 5.95% (C$3,500-74,600), CPP2 4% (to C$85,000) and EI 1.63% employee / 2.282% employer (to C$68,900), and remit on the CRA schedule (accelerated remitters up to 4 times a month; late remittance draws 10% penalties). BC requires pay at least semi-monthly within 8 days after period end and ON a regular recurring payday, both with itemized wage statements; ON/BC Employer Health Tax and WSIB/WorkSafeBC premiums also apply. RSUs at vest, options at exercise and ESPP discounts are withheld on and reported on the T4.
countries.in: Pay before the 7th of the following month with electronic wage slips (Code on Wages s.17(1)), deposit TDS under s.392 of the Income-tax Act 2025 by the 7th, PF (12% + 12% on 'wages', mandatory to INR 25,000/month from 17 Sep 2026) and ESI (to INR 21,000) by the 15th, and Karnataka PT (INR 200/month, INR 300 in February) by the 20th. Compute PF and gratuity on the 50% 'wages' base, and withhold TDS on RSU/ESPP perquisites at vesting or exercise even when the US plan settles the shares.
countries.tw: Pay in NTD on a fixed payday with an itemized statement and no pre-deduction of damages (LSA Arts. 22-23, 26). Deduct the employee shares of Labor Insurance/EI (20%) and NHI (30%), pay the employer shares and the 0.025% wage arrears fund levy, and contribute at least 6% of wage (cap NT$150,000) to each labor pension account. Withhold the 2.11% NHI supplementary premium on bonuses above 4x the monthly insured amount; the minimum wage is NT$29,500/month and NT$196/hour from 1 Jan 2026.
countries.cn: Pay in RMB on a fixed date at least monthly with itemized statements, withhold IIT on the cumulative method and pay by the 15th of the following month, and pay social insurance and housing fund on the actual base within the city floor and cap (Shanghai RMB 7,546-37,731 from 1 Jul 2026). RSU, option and ESPP income is withheld as wages (separate taxation available through 31 Dec 2027) and needs SAFE Circular 7 plan registration; social-insurance waiver agreements are void (SPC Interpretation II Art. 19).

processes.name: Off-cycle & manual payments
processes.summary: Controls payments made outside the regular cycle: final pay, missed or late inputs, underpayment corrections and urgent one-time payments. Off-cycles carry high fraud and SOX risk, so each needs a documented reason, approval by someone other than the requester and processing through the payroll provider with full tax treatment. Good looks like: statutory deadlines met, off-cycles kept rare, and every one traceable to an approved request.
processes.owner: Payroll (process), Finance (approval and SOX control owner), HRBP/People Ops (requesters)
processes.trigger: Approved request for pay that cannot wait for the next regular cycle: statutory final pay, missed input, underpayment correction, urgent one-time payment
outputs: Off-cycle ticket with reason code, calculation and approvals
Off-cycle register and compliant payslip or wage statement
Taxes and statutory contributions withheld and remitted
GL posting included in the cycle reconciliation
Monthly off-cycle log with root-cause analysis
processes.sla: Final pay by the local statutory deadline (CA immediately on discharge); underpayments within 2 business days of approval

steps.label: Off-cycle need identified
steps.detail: HRBP or People Ops raises a ticket with a reason code (final pay, missed input, correction, one-time award), amount basis and pay-by date; managers cannot request directly.

steps.label: Validate request and calculate
steps.detail: Check it is not a duplicate of a regular-cycle payment and calculate gross with the right tax method (US supplemental, Canada bonus method, India TDS, China cumulative IIT). Final pay includes the items local law requires, such as accrued vacation, unused annual leave and meal/rest premiums.

steps.label: Must pay before next cycle?
steps.detail: Required by a statutory deadline or causing real hardship? If not, it moves to the next regular cycle (PY-01).

steps.label: Approve off-cycle payment
steps.detail: Approver is independent of the requester and preparer; the Payroll manager approves up to a set threshold and the Controller above it. Final pay is pre-authorized by policy and reviewed after payment.
steps.control: Independent approval before release

steps.label: Process off-cycle and pay
steps.detail: Provider runs the off-cycle through payroll (not AP) with the same deductions and a payslip. Manual checks or wires are an emergency exception under dual control and are loaded into payroll afterwards.

steps.label: Reconcile and post to GL
steps.detail: Include the off-cycle in the period reconciliation and update statutory reporting (e.g., Canada ROE within 5 calendar days for an interruption of earnings).

steps.label: Report root causes monthly
steps.detail: Monthly log by reason code goes to People Ops and HRBPs; late HRIS input is tracked to the team that caused it.

steps.label: Closed: paid or moved to cycle
steps.detail: Ticket closed with approvals, calculation and payment evidence attached.

controls.control: Independent approval of every off-cycle; approver is not the requester or preparer
controls.evidence: Ticket approval trail with user IDs

controls.control: Finance reviews 100% of the month's off-cycle payments against approved tickets
controls.evidence: Signed monthly off-cycle log

controls.control: Manual checks and wires only under dual control and logged
controls.evidence: Check/wire log with two authorizations

controls.control: Termination date vs final-pay date report by country
controls.evidence: Final-pay timeliness report

kpis.why: Off-cycles are costly and risky
