considerations: Pay employees through payroll, never AP: AP payments skip withholding and W-2/T4 reporting and are a classic audit finding.
Final-pay deadlines drive most urgent off-cycles, so prepare final pay before the termination meeting (CA) rather than after it.
A new bank account followed by an off-cycle request is a fraud red flag; block off-cycles to bank details changed within the last few days unless verified by call-back.
In CA, waiting-time penalties of up to 30 days' wages make a late off-cycle far more expensive than the effort of doing it on time.
Batch non-urgent one-time payments (spot awards, referral bonuses) into a scheduled monthly special run instead of one-off payments.

variations.how: Calculate and approve before the exit date; include accrued vacation, commissions due under the plan and any premiums; deliver on the local deadline.
Used only when the provider cannot meet a statutory deadline; dual control, then load into payroll for tax reporting in the same period.
Pay within 2 business days with a corrected wage statement; include statutory premiums where due.
Requires Total Rewards approval as well as Finance; default is the next regular or monthly special run.

countries.us: Use the supplemental method (22% flat, mandatory 37% over $1M) or the aggregate method and report through the W-2; final-pay deadlines are set by state law, from immediate (CA, CO, MA involuntary) to the next regular payday (NY, IL).
countries.us-ca: On discharge or layoff all wages including accrued vacation are due immediately; on resignation, within 72 hours without notice or on the last day with 72+ hours' notice (LC 201-203), and late final pay accrues waiting-time penalties of up to 30 days' wages. Every off-cycle needs an LC 226-compliant wage statement.
countries.ca: ON final pay is due by the later of 7 days after termination or the next regular payday; BC within 48 hours if the employer terminates or 6 days if the employee quits. Issue the electronic ROE within 5 calendar days after the end of the pay period with the interruption of earnings.
countries.in: Final wages on resignation, dismissal or retrenchment are due within 2 working days (Code on Wages s.17(2)) and gratuity within 30 days of becoming payable; withhold TDS under s.392 on off-cycle salary and perquisites.
countries.tw: Wages, including unused annual leave, must be settled immediately on termination (Enforcement Rules Art. 9; LSA Art. 38) and severance within 30 days; apply the 2.11% NHI supplementary premium to large bonus payments.
countries.cn: Final wages are due in full at termination (verify any short Shenzhen grace period) and economic compensation is paid when the handover is completed (LCL Art. 50); an off-cycle annual bonus can use separate one-off bonus taxation once per year through 31 Dec 2027.

processes.name: Time, attendance & overtime
processes.summary: Captures working time for non-exempt and hours-regulated employees, approves overtime within legal caps, and pays premiums correctly in each country. For an engineering-heavy company the main risks are misclassification and unrecorded after-hours work (tape-outs, calls with US HQ, lab shifts). Good looks like: every hours-regulated employee records time daily, overtime is pre-approved within caps, and premiums are paid in the period earned.
processes.owner: Payroll (process and calculation), Manager (approval), HRBP (policy, caps and remediation), People Ops (classification data)
processes.trigger: Each workday for time capture; each pay-period close for approval and transfer to payroll
outputs: Daily time records (to the minute where required) for hours-regulated employees
Overtime pre-approvals and employee consent where required
Approved timesheets transferred to payroll
Overtime and meal/rest premium calculations
Cap and exception report with remediation
China special working-hours approvals and Taiwan labor-management overtime consents
processes.sla: Timesheets approved within 1 business day of period close; premiums paid in the pay period in which earned

steps.label: Record start, end and breaks
steps.detail: Clock in and out daily in Timekeeping, including remote work and pre-shift log-in, and record meal breaks; no automatic break deductions.

steps.label: Pre-approve overtime within caps
steps.detail: Approve overtime before it is worked and check the local cap (e.g., Taiwan 46 h/month, China 36 h/month). Unapproved overtime that was worked is still paid, then handled as a conduct issue.

steps.label: Attest timesheet
steps.detail: Employee attests the time is complete and accurate, reports any missed or late meal or rest break (which triggers a CA premium) and confirms no off-the-clock work.

steps.label: Approve timesheet
steps.detail: Approve by period close; any manager edit needs a reason code and the employee's acknowledgment.
steps.control: Edit audit trail on every manager change

steps.label: Calculate premiums and load
steps.detail: Apply weekly (US), daily (CA), per-hour-band (Taiwan) or percentage (China, India) overtime rules with the correct regular-rate or base definition, plus meal/rest premiums. Isolate the FLSA overtime premium for W-2 code TT.

steps.label: Run cap and exception report
steps.detail: Flag employees over statutory caps, missing punches, meal-break violations, manager edits and exempt staff logging overtime-type patterns.
steps.control: Monthly cap and exception report reviewed by HRBP

steps.label: Cap breach or pattern found?
steps.detail: HRBP reviews the report with the Dept Head for sites and teams over thresholds.

steps.label: Remediate staffing, approvals, filings
steps.detail: Rebalance workload or add shifts, coach the manager, renew Taiwan labor-management consents and filings, seek China comprehensive-hours approval for shift roles, and send any exemption doubts to Legal.

steps.label: Time paid and records retained
steps.detail: Retain time records for the local period: US 3 years (timecards 2), CA 3 years, Taiwan 5 years, China at least 2 years with the burden of proof on the employer.

controls.control: Timekeeping enforces meal-break attestation and has no automatic break deduction
controls.evidence: System configuration record and attestation logs

controls.control: Monthly review of manager time edits
controls.evidence: Edit report with reviewer sign-off

controls.control: Monthly overtime cap and exception report
controls.evidence: Signed report with remediation actions

controls.control: Annual classification review of job codes (exempt, 'worker', special hours)
controls.evidence: Review memo approved by Legal

kpis.name: Timesheets approved on time
kpis.why: Late approvals cause off-cycles and missed premiums

kpis.name: Employees over statutory overtime caps (TW, CN, IN)
kpis.why: Cap breaches carry fines and signal burnout

kpis.name: Manual time edits per 100 timesheets
kpis.why: High edit rates suggest off-the-clock risk

kpis.name: Wage-hour claims or agency findings
kpis.why: Outcome measure of the whole process

considerations: Classification is the root cause of most exposure: CA exempt floors ($70,304; computer professional $58.85/hr), no salary-based exemption in Taiwan, individual-contributor engineers who may be 'workers' in India, and China roles on standard hours unless approved otherwise.
Evening calls with US HQ from Taiwan or India are working time; in Taiwan, recorded attendance is presumed working time (Labor Incident Act Art. 38), so meeting norms matter.
Only the FLSA-required premium counts as qualified overtime for W-2 code TT; CA daily-only or contractual overtime does not, so payroll must split the codes all year.
Plan tape-out and lab crunches: Taiwan comp time only at the employee's choice with unused hours paid, and CA alternative workweeks only after a secret-ballot election and DLSE filing.
Biometric time clocks need extra care: China facial recognition needs separate consent and a non-biometric alternative, and US state biometric laws (e.g., IL BIPA) apply to remote sites.

variations.how: No time recording for pay, but record project time where it supports R&D credits (e.g., Canada SR&ED timesheets).

CA alternative workweek, China comprehensive-hours approval, and the Karnataka 24x7 notification conditions (10 h/day including overtime, 50 overtime hours per quarter, women's night-shift consent and transport).
Daily time entry, pay for short breaks under 20 minutes, and apply the work state's meal and rest rules.

variations.when: Business travel and fab or customer site visits
variations.how: Apply compensable travel-time rules for non-exempt staff and record hours in Taiwan and China as normal working time.

countries.us: Non-exempt staff get 1.5x over 40 hours a week, with the regular rate including non-discretionary bonuses and shift differentials (29 U.S.C. 207(e)); pay for all hours including pre-shift log-in and breaks under 20 minutes. Exempt status needs $684/week (HCE $107,432) plus the duties test, with higher state thresholds (CA, NY, WA, CO).
countries.us-ca: Pay 1.5x after 8 hours a day or 40 a week and for the first 8 hours on the 7th consecutive day, and 2x after 12 hours or after 8 on the 7th day (LC 510). Provide a 30-minute meal break before the end of the 5th hour and 10-minute rest per 4 hours, with one hour of premium pay at the regular rate per missed break (LC 226.7).
countries.ca: ON pays 1.5x after 44 hours a week, with a maximum of 8 hours a day and 48 a week unless agreed in writing; BC pays 1.5x after 8 hours a day or 40 a week and 2x after 12 hours a day. ON IT professionals and BC high-technology professionals (ESR s.37.8) are exempt, but technicians and support staff usually are not.
countries.in: Workers get 2x the ordinary rate beyond 8 hours a day or 48 a week, only with consent, and central rules cap overtime at 144 hours per quarter; the Karnataka 24x7 notification allows 10 hours a day including overtime and 50 overtime hours per quarter. Individual-contributor engineers are often 'workers' (only managerial staff and supervisors over INR 18,000 are excluded).
countries.tw: Maximum 12 hours a day including overtime and 46 hours a month (54 a month and 138 a quarter with union or labor-management-meeting consent, filed with the authority at 30+ employees), at 1-1/3x for weekday hours 1-2 and 1-2/3x for hours 3-4. Record attendance to the minute and keep it 5 years; recorded time is presumed working time (Labor Incident Act Art. 38).
countries.cn: Overtime is capped at 36 hours a month after consulting the union and employee and paid at 150/200/300% using the 21.75 (daily) or 174 (hourly) divisors; Shanghai's 2026 measures exclude year-end bonus and certain allowances from the overtime base. Flexible or comprehensive hours for FAE, senior or shift/test roles need local HR bureau approval, otherwise standard overtime rules apply.

processes.name: Year-end & statutory payroll filings
processes.summary: Closes each payroll year and produces employee tax statements and statutory returns on time in every country: W-2/W-3 and ACA 1095-C (US), T4/RL-1 (Canada), Form 130 and quarterly Form 138 (India), withholding statements (Taiwan) and IIT annual reconciliation support (China). Good looks like: year-to-date data reconciled before filing, every form issued and filed by its deadline, and no penalty notices.
processes.owner: Payroll (process), Finance/Tax (review and sign-off), Benefits (ACA data), Stock Admin (equity income true-up)
processes.trigger: Q4 year-end readiness review for calendar-year countries; Q4 of the India tax year ending 31 March
outputs: YTD reconciliation of payroll register to quarterly returns and GL
Employee statements: W-2 (with codes TT, TP, TA and Box 14b), 1095-C, T4/RL-1, Form 130, Taiwan withholding statements
Filed returns and transmittals (W-3, 1094-C, T4 Summary, Form 138, Taiwan withholding filing)
Correction log (W-2c, amended T4, revised Form 138)
China IIT annual reconciliation support data
processes.sla: W-2 by Jan 31; 1095-C furnished by about Mar 2 and e-filed by Mar 31; T4/RL-1 by the last day of February; India Form 130 by 15 June; Taiwan filing by 31 Jan and employee statements by 10 Feb; China reconciliation window 1 Mar-30 Jun

steps.label: Start Q4 year-end readiness
steps.detail: Country checklists: address and tax ID clean-up (SSN, SIN, PAN), provider form versions (new W-2 codes), and a final cut-off for taxable benefits, imputed income and relocation.

steps.label: True-up equity income
steps.detail: Reconcile equity platform releases, exercises and ESPP disqualifying dispositions to payroll YTD by country and jurisdiction; issue Forms 3921/3922 by Jan 31.
steps.control: Equity-to-payroll YTD tie-out signed before filing

steps.label: Deliver ACA and benefit data
steps.detail: Offer-of-coverage codes and affordability safe harbor for 1095-C, plus HSA, dependent care FSA (cap $7,500 from 2026), group-term life imputed income and any Trump account contributions (code TA).

steps.label: Reconcile YTD to returns and GL
steps.detail: Tie W-2 totals to the four Forms 941, T4 totals to CRA remittances, Form 138 quarters to TDS deposits and Taiwan annual withholding to monthly deposits, then to the GL.
steps.control: YTD-to-returns-to-GL reconciliation before release

steps.label: Review and approve for filing
steps.detail: Tax reviewer signs the reconciliation and clears the exception list (negative wages, missing IDs, code TT isolation, multi-state splits) before release.

steps.label: Issue statements and file returns
steps.detail: Issue and file by each deadline, with e-delivery only where the employee consented; include RL-1 for Quebec staff and T4A for contractors and other payments.

steps.label: Review statement and raise queries
steps.detail: Employees check statements and raise queries through the ticketing portal. China employees complete their IIT annual reconciliation, and India employees report foreign shares in Schedule FA.

steps.label: Corrections needed?
steps.detail: Based on employee queries, provider notices and post-filing checks.

steps.label: Issue corrected forms
steps.detail: W-2c/W-3c, amended T4 or revised Form 138/130 with a root-cause note; correct configuration before the next year.

steps.label: Year closed; records retained
steps.detail: Retain records for the local period: US payroll tax 4 years, CRA 6 years, India 6+ years, Taiwan wage records 5 years, China payroll accounting vouchers 30 years.

controls.control: YTD register reconciled to quarterly returns and the GL before filing
controls.evidence: Signed reconciliation per country

controls.control: Equity income in payroll reconciled to the equity platform for the year
controls.evidence: Tie-out workpaper

controls.control: Independent Finance/Tax approval before statements are released
controls.evidence: Approval record

controls.control: Filing-deadline tracker with filing acknowledgments
controls.evidence: Tracker with receipts

kpis.name: Forms issued and filed by the statutory deadline
kpis.why: Late filing brings per-form penalties

kpis.name: Corrections per 1,000 statements
kpis.why: Measures year-round data quality

kpis.name: Penalty notices received
kpis.why: Outcome measure

considerations: The new W-2 code TT cannot be fixed in January: the FLSA overtime premium must be isolated in every cycle of the year (IRS transition relief covered 2025 only).
India renumbered its forms under the Income-tax Act 2025: Form 16 is now Form 130 and 24Q is now 138, while FY 2025-26 amounts stay under the 1961 Act, so check provider templates carefully.
Mobile employees and equity need multi-state and cross-border sourcing of RSU income, and Canadian option benefits need the C$200,000 stock-option deduction cap applied.
For ACA, affordability for 2026 is 9.96%; on-request furnishing is allowed for non-full-time individuals, and CA, NJ, MA, RI and DC have their own individual-mandate reporting.
In China the employer mainly supports the employee's reconciliation, but cumulative withholding restarts in January and the separate-bonus-taxation choice must be made per employee.

variations.how: Combine YTD from both providers into one statement per employee and reconcile both sets of returns.
Use last known addresses and furnish a W-2 within 30 days of a written request if the employee does not expect to be rehired that year.
RL-1 slips and QPP/QPIP reporting in addition to the T4.
Report in both home and host countries with tax-equalization reconciliation before statements are issued.

countries.us: Furnish W-2s and file with SSA by Jan 31, including the new 2026 codes TT (qualified overtime), TP (tips) and TA (Trump account contributions) and the Box 14b occupation code; furnish 1095-C by about Mar 2, e-file 1094-C/1095-C by Mar 31, and furnish Forms 3921/3922 by Jan 31.
countries.us-ca: Report CA wages and SDI withholding on the W-2 and reconcile to the EDD quarterly DE 9/DE 9C filings (verify due dates); self-insured plans send Forms 1094/1095 to the Franchise Tax Board by 31 Mar for the state individual mandate.
countries.ca: Issue T4 slips (and T4A for contractors and other payments) and file them with the summary by the last day of February, electronically above 5 slips; Quebec employees also need RL-1 slips. Report equity income with the correct T4 codes and apply the C$200,000 stock-option deduction cap for large non-CCPC employers.
countries.in: Issue Form 130 (formerly Form 16) by 15 June and Form 123 (formerly 12BA) for perquisites, after quarterly Form 138 (formerly 24Q) returns due 31 Jul, 31 Oct, 31 Jan and 31 May; FY 2025-26 amounts stay under the 1961 Act.
countries.tw: File the prior year's income tax withholding and NHI supplementary premium statements with the tax authority by 31 January (next business day if a holiday) and give statements to employees by 10 February; employees file their returns 1-31 May, when foreign professionals claim the special tax incentive.
countries.cn: IIT is withheld cumulatively each month and restarts in January; employees complete the annual reconciliation between 1 March and 30 June through the Individual Income Tax app, and the employer supplies data or files on their behalf where authorized. Decide per employee whether the annual one-off bonus is taxed separately (available through 31 Dec 2027).

processes.name: Payroll error correction & overpayment recovery
processes.summary: Corrects payroll errors fast and recovers overpayments lawfully in each country. Underpayments are fixed first because wage penalties accrue; overpayments are recovered only with the documentation, consent and deduction limits local law requires. Good looks like: underpayments paid within 2 business days, a signed repayment agreement before any deduction, and root causes fixed so errors do not repeat.
processes.owner: Payroll (process), HRBP (employee communication), Legal (recovery method outside standard templates), Finance (write-off approval)
processes.trigger: Error found through an employee query, PY-01 variance review, audit, or late processing of a termination or pay change
outputs: Error ticket with root cause and affected periods
Corrected payment or recovery calculation (gross vs net, tax-year impact)
Signed repayment agreement or deduction authorization
Corrected wage statements and tax forms (W-2c, amended T4, revised Form 138)
Write-off approval where recovery is waived
processes.sla: Underpayments paid within 2 business days of confirmation (via PY-02); overpayment notice to the employee within 5 business days of confirmation

steps.label: Error reported or detected
steps.detail: Ticket logged with source (employee, variance review, audit) and first estimate of impact.

steps.label: Investigate and quantify
steps.detail: Identify cause and affected periods and calculate gross, net, taxes, social insurance and any equity impact. Note whether the error crosses a tax year, which changes gross vs net recovery and form corrections.

steps.label: Underpaid or overpaid?
steps.detail: Direction of the error decides the path; mixed cases are split.

steps.label: Pay shortfall off-cycle
steps.detail: Pay through PY-02 with a corrected wage statement, including statutory premiums or penalties where due (e.g., CA meal/rest premiums, waiting time on final pay).

steps.label: Notify employee in writing
steps.detail: Explain the overpayment, amount (gross and net), cause and repayment options (lump sum or installments over at least the period overpaid). No deduction is made at this stage.

steps.label: Confirm lawful recovery method
steps.detail: Standard country templates cover routine cases; Legal reviews exceptions such as recovery from final pay, large amounts, CA and China, or disputed balances.

steps.label: Agree repayment plan
steps.detail: Employee signs a deduction authorization (amount and schedule) or repays directly; disputes escalate to the HRBP.

steps.label: Recover or write off?
steps.detail: Write off when cost exceeds value, there is hardship, or no lawful recovery route or consent exists; thresholds set by the Controller.

steps.label: Process deductions and tax fixes
steps.detail: Deduct within local limits and only under the signed authorization. Adjust tax reporting: same-year errors correct wages; prior-year errors need W-2c or amended slips.
steps.control: Recovery deduction code requires a linked signed authorization

steps.label: Root cause fixed; case closed
steps.detail: Configuration or process fix recorded, SOX impact assessed, and any written-off amount reported as income where required.

controls.control: No overpayment deduction without a signed authorization linked to the deduction code
controls.evidence: E-signed authorization referenced on the deduction record

controls.control: Write-offs approved against Controller thresholds
controls.evidence: Approval record per write-off

controls.control: Monthly error log with root-cause review
controls.evidence: Signed error log and action list

controls.control: Termination-processing timeliness report to prevent post-exit pay
controls.evidence: Report of terminations entered after the last day worked

kpis.name: Underpayments corrected within 2 business days
kpis.why: Wage penalties and trust both depend on speed

kpis.name: Agreed overpayment amounts recovered within 6 months
kpis.why: Measures recovery effectiveness

kpis.name: Overpayments caused by late terminations
kpis.why: Most preventable error source

kpis.name: Repeat errors with the same root cause within 12 months
kpis.why: Tests whether fixes stick

considerations: Late terminations cause most overpayments, and erroneous vesting too; enforce a termination-entry deadline tied to the last day worked.

Gross vs net matters: same-year recoveries are usually net with a wage correction, while prior-year recoveries are gross with corrected forms and more employee tax complexity. Get Tax input before quoting an amount.
The overpayment is the employer's error: offer installments at least as long as the overpayment period, and keep a hardship waiver path.
Never self-help from CA final pay, and remember that many US states limit recovery deductions even with consent.
Equity over-vesting or withholding errors cannot simply be reversed; involve Stock Admin and Tax on share return vs cash repayment.

variations.how: No payroll to deduct from: send a written demand and invoice, and write off small balances under the threshold.

variations.when: Systemic configuration error affecting many employees
variations.how: Legal-reviewed mass communication, correction run, and assessment of class or PAGA exposure for underpayments.
Follow plan rules and catch-up limits for missed premiums; coordinate with Benefits.
Stock Admin and Tax correct through the next payroll or a cash settlement; the vest itself is not unwound.

countries.us: Recovery deductions cannot take a non-exempt employee below minimum wage, and many states require written, voluntary authorization or restrict self-help recovery (e.g., NY Labor Law 193, 820 ILCS 115/9, WA); prior-year overpayments need a W-2c for Social Security and Medicare wages.
countries.us-ca: Deduct only with lawful authorization and never from final pay without it; deductions for losses are barred unless caused by dishonesty, willful act or gross negligence (LC 221, 224; Wage Order 4). Underpaid final pay accrues waiting-time penalties of up to 30 days' wages (LC 203), so fix underpayments first.
countries.ca: Deductions from wages need the employee's written authorization and statutory permission (ON ESA s.13; BC ESA ss.21-22), so get signed consent for the specific amount before recovering through payroll, and correct CPP/EI and the T4 for the affected year.
countries.in: Payroll recovery must fall within the authorised deductions in Code on Wages s.18, with total deductions capped at 50% of wages; recovery from final pay needs clear contract terms and still carries litigation risk.
countries.tw: Wages must be paid in full and damages cannot be pre-deducted (LSA Arts. 22, 26), so recover overpayments by written agreement or separate repayment rather than unilateral offset, with unjust enrichment under Civil Code Art. 179 as the fallback (verify).
countries.cn: Deductions for employee-caused losses are capped at 20% of monthly wage and cannot take pay below the local minimum wage; recover overpayments only with the employee's written agreement, with unjust enrichment (Civil Code Art. 985) as the fallback (verify).
